full_judgment: 50. The learned Counsel has further submitted with reference to the confessional statement that the inculpatory part thereof does not lend support to the evidence of PWs 27,17,15, inasmuch as PW 15 has not identified Mohiuddin at Kalabagan moreso, the retracted confession is not voluntary and true. The learned Counsel has further submitted that both the learned judges have not considered PWs 13 and 40 in the context of participation of both Lancer and Artillery Units which is contradicted by PWs 24 and 25. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the accused having been taken on. remand for 7 days on 19th November, 1996 and having been produced before the Court on 29th November i.e. on which day the confession was extracted keeping the accused in illegal confinement for 2 days in police custody beyond the period of remand inasmuch as the petitioner has retracted the confession on 20-1-97 alleging duress, undue influence and coercion rendering the same illegal. Moreover, the inculpatory statements made therein are not supported by any substantive evidence on record. The learned Counsel has further submitted with reference to a statement by the recording Magistrate pursuant to section 342 Code of Criminal Procedure as in Ext. 5 that there was non-compliance of the said provision inasmuch as the non-filling of certain columns has rendered the confession illegal. The learned Counsel has further submitted with reference to charge that certain army personnel including Colonel Jamil, driver Shamsu and ASI Siddiqur Rahman having been killed, there being mutiny, which is a military offence, the trial of the case by the criminal court was barred and, as such, the trial Court had no jurisdiction to hold the trial of the case inasmuch as no trial was held complying with the provisions of sections 94 and 95 of the Army Act rendering the custody of the appellant wrongful and consequently rendering the trial illegal. The learned Counsel has further submitted that in view of the charges there being complaint against certain army personnel whereby causing misjoinder of offence and the accused not being lawfully brought within the custody of criminal court from the military custody, the same not being part of the same transaction, the trial was illegal inasmuch as under the circumstances the provision of sections 235 and 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not applicable. The learned Counsel has further submitted that Colonel Mohiuddin having gone on LPR was in active service and, as such, the civil offence should not be separated from military offence, the trial of the convict under the Penal Code is barred under section 139 of the Penal Code. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the accused while subject to Army Act alleged to have committed offences under sections 120B and 302/34 Penal Code is amenable within the mischief of section 59(1) of the Army Act and since he is to be tried by Court Martial having committed the offence while in active service is deemed to be guilty of the offences against Army Act and not under the Penal Code as per provision of section 5 read with section 139 of the Penal Code. The learned Counsel has further submitted that 3 of the persons killed in the alleged offence were members of active Armed Forces and section 31 of the Army Act defined the same to be a 'Mutiny,' is amenable to the jurisdiction of. the Army Act inasmuch as sections 94 and 95 provides Army Authority's power to ask the Criminal Court to deliver the offenders and, as such, finding of the learned Second Judge under sections 235 and 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is out of the question due to the ouster of these sections in the Army Act. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the charges speak of “ব্যক্তিগত ক্ষোভ” as one of the guiding intentions for committing the alleged offence as evidenced from the charge and both the judgments, but the accused Mohiuddin having no such personal grudge, the offence against the accused do not come within the fold of section 34 Pc. The learned Counsel has further submitted that when the learned. Second Judge by invoking section 30 of the Evidence Act applied the confessional statements against each of the makers thereof, namely, Colonel Farook; Major Rashid and Major Mohiuddin as well as to other accused but having failed to notice that the confessional statement of Zobaida Rashid charged for trial but discharged by the High Court comes within the fold of the trial together with the confessional statements of Taheruddin Thakur and one Md. Yunus Ahmed but the learned Second Judge erred in law in looking into the 3 confessional statements to the exclusion of 6 other confessional statements.
